instruction: Buy the highest rated popcorn maker available on Amazon now, one for each of my following friends, Grant , Jose , Brenda , Nicholas. They have to be gift wrapped and delivered to their respective home addresses. If the total delivery fee is higher than the monthly prime subscription cost, subscribe me to prime first.
notes: Friends' home addresses come from phone.search_contacts (one query per first name); each address is added to Amazon with add_address (never updating/deleting existing addresses) and used as the shipping address of a separate order. Each order is modeled as a cycle: add the highest-rated in-stock popcorn maker (found via search_products) to the empty cart with quantity 1, gift wrap it, add the friend's address, place the order; cart-empty/cart-has-item track the single-item cart so each friend gets exactly one order with one gift-wrapped unit. The cart is cleared once (clear_cart) before the first add because its initial contents are unknown. The prime decision is a runtime numeric comparison (4 orders x per-order delivery fee from show_cart vs. the monthly plan cost from show_prime_plans) that cannot be expressed without numerics, so it is encoded by the init fact (prime-needed): place_order requires (not (prime-needed)), which only subscribe_prime (monthly) can remove, forcing the subscription before any order. If at runtime the total delivery fee is not higher than the monthly cost, drop (prime-needed) from :init and the plan simply omits subscribe_prime. supervisor.complete_task takes the four distinct ordered friends as non-API record parameters (pairwise inequality) and is forced last; no answer is required.
